name: Hellenic League of the Lamian War

predecessors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
predecessors.text: the Greek states that 'revolted after Alexander's death': Athens, the Aetolians, Thessaly, Phocis, Locris and the Peloponnesian allies

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: Thessaly recovered after Crannon (6 August 322), Athens garrisoned at Munychia (18 September 322) and stripped of 'possessions outside Attica' (Oropus, Samos)

successors.name: Aetolian League
successors.text: Aetolia, which 'was the only state to continue the war' and was never reduced (Antipater and Craterus's Aetolian campaign of 322/321 was abandoned)

ledger.x: September 323: 'Athens was already preparing for war when the news of Alexander's death in June 323 BC became known'; 'war started shortly after, probably in the beginning of September'; the Aetolian 'alliance was possibly concluded in mid-September 323 BC'.
September 323 to August 322: rule 6 blend over the fighting zone.
27 October 323: 'the treaty between Athens and Phokis is dated from 27 October'.
23 December 323: 'Sicyon's treaty with Athens is dated 23 December'.
6 August 322: 'The final battle took place at Crannon on 6 August 322 BC' (Heckel gives 5 August), a Macedonian victory; the Greek cities then made separate terms.
August 322: after Crannon Antipater took the Thessalian and central Greek cities one by one as they 'made separate terms'.
18 September 322: Munychia 'was thus taken on 18 September 322 BC'.
September 322: the alliance is over with Athens's surrender; Hypereides was killed on 6 October and Demosthenes a week later.

wars.name: Lamian War
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory': Thessaly recovered, Athens garrisoned and disfranchised, the Greek allies made separate terms; only the Aetolians held out.

certainty.note: An alliance of states drawn as one hatch: member lists are firm, their tribal boundaries approximate, and the Peloponnesian members joined over the winter.
